question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ -19 & -15 & -1\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}a & ∗ & ∗ \\ b & ∗ & ∗ \\ c & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $\frac{b}{c}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ may be written as a composition of Jordan blocks, as follows:

$$
J={J}_{2}(3)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(-1)
$$

So, we have

- a single $2\times 2$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =3,$ and

- a single $1\times 1$ block corresponding to $\lambda =-1.$

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chains: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(3) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-3I\,}{\to }0 &  \\ {J}_{1}(-1) & : & {v}_{3}\overset{A+I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the first column of $P$ is an eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda =3.$ 

Now, computing $A-3I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 0 \\ -19 & -15 & -1\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -19 & -15 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -19 & -15 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-19){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}-({x}_{3})=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{1}{1}=1.$
